elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "each Party's total aggregate liability ... shall not exceed the greater of ..." plus "The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims." Both directions are capped; no residual unlimited-Customer-liability language remains (deterministic check confirms).

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.1 gives "the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000." The amount, basis and floor are correct and the illusory defined "Fees"/first-Order-Form limitation is cured, but the lookback is anchored to the event giving rise to the claim rather than to the claim as the element literally requires; the deterministic check "preferred cap lookback precedes the claim" returns false. Repair: change the temporal anchor to "the twelve (12) months preceding the claim."

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.2 (untouched): "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill" — expressly mutual.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 defines Excluded Claims to include "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations", and 21.1 caps liability "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: Excluded Claims include "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations"; carved out of the 21.1 cap.
21.3: "its indemnification obligations" is an Excluded Claim, outside the 21.1 cap.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" listed as Excluded Claims.
21.3: "... or fraud" is within the Excluded Claims definition carved out of the cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Rendered 21.3 now reads "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed amounts due for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section." Substituting "amounts due" for the illusory defined "Fees" is an improvement, but the carve-out still reaches only undisputed amounts for conforming Services rather than Customer's payment obligations as a whole; the deterministic check "preferred payment carve-out covers Customer payment obligations" is false. Repair: state that Customer's obligations to pay amounts due under this Agreement and any Order Form are not damages subject to this Section (the drafter may keep an undisputed-amounts qualifier only if it is acceptable that disputed-but-owed amounts fall inside the cap).

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1 caps "each Party's total aggregate liability" and expressly states "The cap is mutual".

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as rendered uses "the fees paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement and all Order Forms during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim", with a USD 1,000,000 floor. Lowercase "fees" plus "all Order Forms" defeats the illusory defined term (Fees = one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee under the first Order Form), so the cap is genuinely a 12-month fee basis. The fallback element imposes no specific anchor, so the event-based lookback does not defeat it.
21.3 Excluded Claims include "its indemnification obligations"; 21.1 opens "Except for Excluded Claims".

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims include "a Party's breach of confidentiality ... obligations".

reasons: The finding status "deviation" is correct on the original text: the cap keyed to defined "Fees" (the one-time USD 12,000 Implementation Fee) and further limited to the first Order Form is illusory and sits well below six months' fees, i.e. walk-away territory, so a redline was warranted.

The redline is position-complete at the fallback level: mutual cap, a genuine 12-month fee basis (with a USD 1,000,000 floor), and uncapped indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct all appear in operative language.

It is not complete at the claimed preferred level for two reasons. (1) The cap lookback runs from "the event giving rise to the claim" rather than from the claim as the preferred element literally specifies (deterministic check false); fix by writing "the twelve (12) months preceding the claim". (2) The payment carve-out in 21.3 still reaches only "undisputed amounts due for conforming Services", a subset rather than Customer's payment obligations as a whole (deterministic check false); fix by excluding Customer's obligation to pay amounts due under this Agreement and any Order Form from damages subject to this Section.

Minimality holds: only two surgical edits were made — the cap formula in 21.1 and the noun in the 21.3 payment carve-out. Replacing capitalised "Fees" with lowercase "fees" and expanding "the first Order Form" to "this Agreement and all Order Forms" is necessary, not cosmetic, because the defined term renders the cap illusory. No survival tails, expense language, procedures or extra damages categories were added, and the favourable retained language in 21.2 (restoration, replacement services, notice and incident-response costs as direct damages) and the full Excluded Claims list are untouched.

Intent is preserved: definitions 1.5/1.6 remain in place for the payment provisions that use them, so no term is left undefined and no cross-reference dangles; the mutual damages exclusion, the form-of-action language and the conforming-Services/undisputed qualifiers survive without contradiction. No new Vendor-favourable exception or requirement outside the checklist was introduced.

Drafting note for the margin comment: it accurately describes both edits and the playbook position, but it should not be read as delivering the preferred position in full given the two residual gaps above.
